title: A strict interval-attachment model for derived simplicial localization
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the Dwyer--Kan model structure, its cofibrations, the homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$, and derived localization $L_VD$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], in fixed containing universes. Let $[1]$ be the discrete two-object walking arrow, and $\mathbb J$ the discrete two-object groupoid with exactly one arrow between each ordered pair. Fix a factorization $[1]\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J$ of the arrow-to-isomorphism functor with $i$ a cofibration and $r$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Such a factorization exists, and $K$ is cofibrant. For a small simplicial category $D$, a small set $V$, and a specified vertex arrow $v$ of $D$ for each label $v\in V$, define the ordinary pushout
$$\Gamma(D,V)=D\amalg_{\coprod_{v\in V}[1]}\coprod_{v\in V}K.$$
The canonical map $D\to\Gamma(D,V)$ represents $D\to L_VD$ under a natural isomorphism $\Gamma(D,V)\cong L_VD$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ under $D$. The construction is a strict functor on pairs: a simplicial functor $F:D\to D'$ and a label function $s:V\to V'$ with $F(v)=s(v)$ induce a map of pushouts, respecting identities and composition. If $s$ is the identity of a common label set and $F$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, the induced $\Gamma(D,V)\to\Gamma(D',V)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. If a simplicial functor $g:D\to T$ sends all labelled arrows to identity vertices, it has a specified extension $\bar g:\Gamma(D,V)\to T$: on the copy of $K$ for $v$, use $K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J\to\{g(\operatorname{source}v)\}\to T$. These extensions are natural for maps of pairs and for postcomposition by simplicial functors.
